verses.sanskrit: उपक्रम्यस्य हि द्वित्वाद्विधैवोपक्रमो मतः । एकः सन्तर्पणस्तत्र द्वितीयश्चापतर्पणः ॥१॥
verses.student_meaning: All therapeutic intervention is broadly of two kinds: Santarpana, which nourishes, and Apatarpana, which reduces excessive nourishment.

verses.sanskrit: बृंहणो लङ्घनश्चेति तत्पर्यायावुदाहृतौ । बृंहणं यद्गुरुत्वाय लङ्घनं लाघवाय यत् ॥२॥
verses.student_meaning: Brimhana and Langhana are synonyms for the two approaches; Brimhana promotes bodily heaviness/fullness while Langhana produces lightness.

verses.sanskrit: स्नेहनं रूक्षणं कर्म स्वेदनं स्तम्भनं च यत् । भूतानां तदपि द्वैध्याद्द्वितयं नातिवर्तते ॥३॥
verses.student_meaning: Snigdha, Ruksha, Svedana and Stambhana actions, though diverse, fall within the two broad therapeutic directions.

verses.sanskrit: शोधनं शमनं चेति द्विधा तत्रापि लङ्घनम् ॥४॥
verses.student_meaning: Langhana itself is divided into Shodhana and Shamana.

verses.sanskrit: यदीरयेद्बहिर्दोषान् पञ्चधा शोधनं च तत् । निरूहो वमनं कायशिरोरेकोऽस्रविस्रुतिः ॥५॥
verses.student_meaning: Shodhana expels doshas outward and is described here in five forms: Niruha, Vamana, Virechana, Shirovirechana and bloodletting.

verses.sanskrit: न शोधयति यद्दोषान् समान्नोदीरयत्यपि । समीकरोति विषमान् शमनं तच्च सप्तधा ॥६॥
verses.student_meaning: Shamana does not forcibly expel doshas; it normalizes imbalance and is described in seven forms.

verses.sanskrit: पाचनं दीपनं क्षुत्तृड्व्यायामातपमारुताः । बृंहणं शमनं त्वेव वायोः पित्तानिलस्य च ॥७॥
verses.student_meaning: The seven Shamana measures are Pachana, Dipana, hunger regulation, thirst regulation, exercise, heat exposure and air exposure; Brimhana is especially useful for Vata and Vata-associated Pitta.

verses.sanskrit: बृंहयेव्याधिभैषज्यमद्यस्त्रीशोककर्शितान् । भाराध्वोरःक्षतक्षीणरूक्षदुर्बलवातलान् ॥८॥
verses.student_meaning: Brimhana is indicated for wasting from disease, alcohol, excessive sexual activity, grief, heavy exertion, long travel, chest injury, dryness, weakness and Vata predominance.

verses.sanskrit: गर्भिणीसूतिकाबालवृद्धान् ग्रीष्मेऽपरानपि । मांसक्षीरसितासर्पिर्मधुरस्निग्धबस्तिभिः ॥९॥
verses.student_meaning: Pregnant women, postpartum women, children, elderly persons and, generally, persons in summer are included among those requiring nourishment; nourishing foods and measures are listed.

verses.sanskrit: स्वप्नशय्यासुखाभ्यङ्गस्नाननिर्वृतिहर्षणैः । मेहामदोषातिस्निग्धज्वरोरुस्तम्भकुष्ठिनः ॥१०॥
verses.student_meaning: Sweet, unctuous nourishment, sleep, massage, bathing, comfort and cheerfulness are described; the next line begins the list of patients for Langhana.

verses.sanskrit: विसर्पविद्रधिप्लीहशिरःकण्ठाक्षिरोगिणः । स्थूलांश्च लङ्घयेन्नित्यं शिशिरे त्वपरानपि ॥११॥
verses.student_meaning: Langhana is indicated in Prameha, Ama, excess unctuousness, fever, Uru-stambha, skin disease, Visarpa, Vidradhi, splenic, head, throat, eye disease and obesity; others may require it in winter.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र संशोधनैः स्थौल्यबलपित्तकफाधिकान् । आमदोषज्वरच्छर्दिरतीसारहृदामयैः ॥१२॥
verses.student_meaning: Stronger purification is suited to marked obesity and strong Pitta/Kapha states, while the strength and disease context determine the approach.

verses.sanskrit: विबन्धगौरवोद्गारहृल्लासादिभिरातुरान् । मध्यस्थौल्यादिकान् प्रायः पूर्वं पाचनदीपनैः ॥१३॥
verses.student_meaning: In moderate states and moderate-strength patients with Ama and related disorders, Pachana and Dipana are used first.

verses.sanskrit: एभिरेवामयैरार्तान् हीनस्थौल्यबलादिकान् । क्षुत्तृष्णानिग्रहैर्दोषैस्त्वार्तान् मध्यबलैर्दृढान् ॥१४॥
verses.student_meaning: In weaker patients, hunger/thirst restraint is used cautiously; stronger moderate-strength patients may receive more active reducing measures.

verses.sanskrit: समीरणातपायासैः किमुताल्पबलान् नरान् । न बृहयेल्लङ्घनीयान् बृंह्यांस्तु मृदु लङ्घयेत् ॥१५॥
verses.student_meaning: Air, heat and exertion are reducing measures; patients requiring Langhana should not be nourished, while those requiring nourishment should receive only mild Langhana.

verses.sanskrit: युक्त्या वा देशकालादिबलतस्तानुपाचरेत् । बृंहिते स्याद्बलं पुष्टिस्तत्साध्यामयसङ्क्षयः ॥१६॥
verses.student_meaning: Treatment must be individualized according to country, season, strength and circumstances; proper Brimhana increases strength and nourishment and reduces suitable disease.

verses.sanskrit: विमलेन्द्रियता सर्गो मलानां लाघवं रुचिः । क्षुत्तृट्सहोदयः शुद्धहृदयोद्गारकण्ठता ॥१७॥
verses.student_meaning: Successful Langhana is marked by clearer senses, easy elimination, lightness, appetite and thirst, cleaner heart/belching/throat, reduced disease, enthusiasm and loss of drowsiness.

verses.sanskrit: व्याधिमार्दवमुत्साहस्तन्द्रानाशश्च लङ्घिते । अनपेक्षितमात्रादिसेविते कुरुतस्तु ते ॥१८॥
verses.student_meaning: Improper quantity or use of either nourishing or reducing measures produces their respective over-effects.

verses.sanskrit: अतिस्थौल्यातिकार्श्यादीन् वक्ष्यन्ते ते च सौषधाः । रूपं तैरेव च ज्ञेयमतिबृंहितलङ्घिते ॥१९॥
verses.student_meaning: The characteristic outcomes of excessive Brimhana and excessive Langhana help identify which therapeutic excess has occurred.

verses.sanskrit: अतिस्थौल्यापचीमेहज्वरोदरभगन्दरान् । काससन्न्यासकृच्छ्रामकुष्ठादीनतिदारुणान् ॥२०॥
verses.student_meaning: Excessive nourishment can lead to obesity, glandular disorders, Prameha, fever, abdominal disease, fistula, cough, collapse, urinary difficulty, Ama-related disease and skin disease.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र मेदोऽनिलश्लेष्मनाशनं सर्वमिष्यते । कुलत्थजूर्णश्यामाकयवमुद्गमधूदकम् ॥२१॥
verses.student_meaning: In such disorders, measures that reduce excessive Medas, Vata and Kapha are advised; pulses, grains, honey-water and related reducing measures are listed.

verses.sanskrit: मस्तुदण्डाहतारिष्टचिन्ताशोधनजागरम् । मधुना त्रिफलां लिह्याद्गुडूचीमभयां घनम् ॥२२॥
verses.student_meaning: Specific formulations and lifestyle measures are described for excessive obesity, including Triphala, Guduchi, Abhaya and related preparations.

verses.sanskrit: रसाञ्जनस्य महतः पञ्चमूलस्य गुग्गुलोः । शिलाजतुप्रयोगश्च साग्निमन्थरसो हितः ॥२३॥
verses.student_meaning: Additional formulations involving Rasanjana, Panchamula, Guggulu, Shilajatu and Agnimantha are described.

verses.sanskrit: विडङ्गं नागरं क्षारः काललोहरजो मधु । यवामलकचूर्णं च योगोऽतिस्थौल्यदोषजित् ॥२४॥
verses.student_meaning: Vidanga, Nagara, alkaline preparations, iron, honey, barley and Amalaki are given as a reducing formulation for excessive obesity.

verses.sanskrit: व्योषकट्वीवराशिग्रुविडङ्गातिविषास्थिराः । हिङ्गुसौवर्चलाजाजीयवानीधान्यचित्रकाः ॥२५॥
verses.student_meaning: A multi-drug formulation beginning with Vyosha, Katvi, Triphala group, Shigru, Vidanga and other drugs is described.

verses.sanskrit: निशे बृहत्यौ हपुषा पाठा मूलं च केम्बुकात् । एषां चूर्णं मधु घृतं तैलं च सदृशांशकम् ॥२६॥
verses.student_meaning: The same formulation is continued with Brihati, Hapusha, Patha, Kembuka and equal portions of honey, ghee and oil.

verses.sanskrit: सक्तुभिः षोडशगुणैर्युक्तं पीतं निहन्ति तत् । अतिस्थौल्यादिकान् सर्वान् रोगानन्यांश्च तद्विधान् ॥२७॥
verses.student_meaning: Taken with sixteen times its quantity of Saktu, the formulation is said to reduce excessive obesity and similar disorders.

verses.sanskrit: हृद्रोगकामलाश्वित्रश्वासकासगलग्रहान् । बुद्धिमेधास्मृतिकरं सन्नस्याग्नेश्च दीपनम् ॥२८॥
verses.student_meaning: It is also described for heart disease, jaundice, leucoderma, dyspnea, cough and throat disorders, and as supportive of intellect, memory and weak digestion.

verses.sanskrit: अतिकायभ्रमः कासस्तृष्णाधिक्यमरोचकः । स्नेहाग्निनिद्रादृक्श्रोत्रशुक्रौजःक्षुत्स्वरक्षयः ॥२९॥
verses.student_meaning: Excessive Langhana can produce marked emaciation, dizziness, cough, excessive thirst and anorexia, with depletion of unctuousness, digestion, sleep, senses, reproductive tissue, Ojas, appetite and voice.

verses.sanskrit: बस्तिहृन्मूर्धजङ्घोरुत्रिकपार्श्वरुजा ज्वरः । प्रलापो निलग्लानिच्छर्दिपर्वास्थिभेदनम् ॥३०॥
verses.student_meaning: Further complications include pain in the bladder, heart, head, thighs, sacrum and flanks, fever, delirium, Vata aggravation, debility, vomiting and bone/joint pain.

verses.sanskrit: वर्चोमूत्रग्रहाद्याश्च जायन्तेऽतिविलङ्घनात् । कार्यमेव वरं स्थौल्यात् न हि स्थूलस्य भेषजम् ॥३१॥
verses.student_meaning: Severe Langhana can produce constipation and urinary obstruction; in obesity, becoming lean is preferable to remaining excessively obese, and no simple single medicine is sufficient.

verses.sanskrit: बृंहणं लङ्घनं वाऽलमतिमेदोऽग्निवातजित् । मधुरस्निग्धसौहित्यैर्यत्सौख्येन च नश्यति ॥३२॥
verses.student_meaning: Neither Brimhana nor Langhana alone is enough to correct every aspect of severe obesity; emaciation is treated with the opposite approach.

verses.sanskrit: क्रशिमा स्थविमा चात्यन्तविपरीतनिषेवणैः । योजयेद्बृंहणं तत्र सर्वं पानान्नभेषजम् ॥३३॥
verses.student_meaning: Emaciation is relieved by sustained intake of sweet, unctuous, satisfying nourishment and comfortable living, while obesity requires prolonged opposite measures.

verses.sanskrit: अचिन्तया हर्षणेन ध्रुवं सन्तर्पणेन च । स्वप्नप्रसङ्गाच्च कृशो वराह इव पुष्यति ॥३४॥
verses.student_meaning: For emaciation, nourishing drinks, foods and medicines are to be systematically employed.

verses.sanskrit: न हि मांससमं किञ्चिदन्यद्देहबृहत्त्वकृत् । मांसादमांसं मांसेन सम्भृतत्वाद्विशेषतः ॥३५॥
verses.student_meaning: Freedom from worry, cheerfulness, nourishment and adequate sleep promote restoration of the emaciated person.

verses.sanskrit: गुरु चातर्पणं स्थूले विपरीतं हितं कृशे । यवगोधूममुभयोस्तद्योग्याहितकल्पनम् ॥३६॥
verses.student_meaning: Among nourishing substances, meat is described as particularly effective for increasing body bulk; meat-eating animals are given as an illustrative example.

verses.sanskrit: दोषगत्याऽतिरिच्यन्ते ग्राहिभेद्यादिभेदतः । उपक्रमा न ते द्वित्वाद्भिन्ना अपि गदा इव ॥३७॥
verses.student_meaning: For obesity, heavy and reducing measures are advised; for emaciation, the opposite is beneficial, with appropriate preparations of barley and wheat.

sections.title: Diseases of Excessive Santarpana and Their Management

learning_outcomes: Define Santarpana, Apatarpana, Brimhana and Langhana.
Differentiate Shodhana and Shamana as forms of Langhana.
Identify indications and contraindications for Brimhana and Langhana.
Recognize signs of adequate and excessive Langhana/Santarpana.
Explain classical management principles for obesity and emaciation.
Understand how specific therapies remain included within the two fundamental Upakrama.
exam_focus: Integration of specialized therapies under Santarpana/Apatarpana.

cross_check: University of Hyderabad SHMT proof-read corpus
source_text.verification_note: Pustak and the cross-checked Sanskrit transmission establish a 37-verse chapter ending with the Chapter 14 colophon. Minor orthographic/compound segmentation differences are normalized to the Sanskrit text while preserving the numbered verse structure.

revision_summary: Make a Santarpana versus Apatarpana comparison table.
Learn indications for Brimhana and Langhana by patient strength and disease state.
Memorize signs of proper Langhana and excess Langhana.
Revise Atisthoulya and Atikarshya management separately.
Remember that specialized therapeutic actions remain within the two fundamental Upakrama.
